subject: music
topicDisplay: Area of Study 1: Western Classical Music 1600-1910
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Approximately which dates define the Baroque period?
questions.explain: The Baroque period runs from roughly 1600 to 1750, ending around the death of J.S. Bach.

questions.q: Which composer is most closely associated with the Baroque period?
questions.explain: J.S. Bach is a central Baroque composer, whereas the others belong to the Classical and Romantic periods.

questions.q: Which keyboard instrument typically played the basso continuo in Baroque music?
questions.explain: The harpsichord commonly realised the basso continuo, filling out the harmony above the bass line.

questions.q: Approximately which dates define the Classical period?
questions.explain: The Classical period spans roughly 1750 to 1810, the era of Haydn, Mozart and early Beethoven.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Romantic music?
options: A wide dynamic range and expressive use of rubato
Terraced dynamics with a harpsichord continuo
Strictly balanced two-bar phrases and Alberti bass
Modal melodies over a single unaccompanied line
questions.explain: Romantic composers favoured extremes of dynamics and flexible rubato to heighten emotional expression.

questions.q: What best describes homophonic texture?
options: A melody supported by chordal accompaniment
Two or more independent melodic lines together
A texture with no clear melody at all
questions.explain: In homophonic texture one clear melody is accompanied by supporting chords.

questions.q: What does a polyphonic (contrapuntal) texture involve?
options: Two or more independent melodic lines woven together
A single melody doubled at the octave
questions.explain: Polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic parts, as in a Baroque fugue.

questions.q: What are the three main sections of sonata form, in order?
questions.explain: Sonata form presents themes in the exposition, transforms them in the development, then restates them in the recapitulation.

questions.q: Which letter pattern represents ternary form?
questions.explain: Ternary form has three sections in which the opening material returns after a contrasting middle section.

questions.q: Which letter pattern best represents rondo form?
questions.explain: In rondo form a recurring main theme (A) alternates with contrasting episodes.

questions.q: What is a ground bass?
options: A repeating bass line over which the upper parts change
A sudden loud chord in the bass register
A bass instrument that plays only the tonic note
A free bass line that never repeats
questions.explain: A ground bass is a short bass pattern repeated continuously while the melody and harmony above it vary.

questions.q: In a Baroque concerto grosso, what is the small group of soloists called?
questions.explain: The concertino is the small group of soloists that contrasts with the fuller ensemble.

questions.q: In a concerto grosso, what name is given to the larger accompanying ensemble?
questions.explain: The ripieno is the larger group that alternates and contrasts with the concertino soloists.

questions.q: Terraced dynamics, where volume shifts suddenly between loud and soft, are most typical of which period?
questions.explain: Baroque music often uses terraced dynamics because instruments such as the harpsichord could not easily produce gradual crescendos.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was added to the orchestra and became standard during the Classical period?
questions.explain: The clarinet was incorporated into the orchestra and became a standard woodwind instrument during the Classical period.

questions.q: A piece uses a harpsichord basso continuo, terraced dynamics and a contrapuntal texture. Which period does it most likely belong to?
questions.explain: Basso continuo, terraced dynamics and counterpoint are all hallmarks of Baroque style.

questions.q: You analyse a movement whose sections run A B A C A D A. Which form is this?
questions.explain: The recurring A theme alternating with contrasting episodes is the defining pattern of rondo form.

questions.q: You hear a single melody performed with no accompaniment. Which texture is this?
questions.explain: A single melodic line with no accompaniment is a monophonic texture.

questions.q: What is a leitmotif, a device developed by Wagner in the Romantic period?
options: A recurring musical theme linked to a character or idea
A sudden change from loud to soft dynamics
A repeating bass line beneath changing harmonies
A cadenza performed by a solo instrument
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a short recurring theme associated with a particular character, object or idea, used prominently by Wagner.

questions.q: A solo piano nocturne written around 1840 features expressive rubato and rich chromatic harmony. Which period does it belong to?
questions.explain: The date, expressive rubato and chromatic harmony are all characteristic of the Romantic period.
